claim: concentrating 600 mergeable drops into a 3x3 block does not regress the bucketed merge, because the pile collapses to one stack on the first tick
measurement: same runner and release build, 3 processes. drop_pile: 600 drops in a 3x3 block plus 600 spread over 12 blocks = 10272us per tick, drop stage 0.3ms (3 percent). entity_heavy for reference: 337607us, drop stage 148.3ms (44 percent).
why: a concentrated pile merges into a single stack on the first tick, so the bucket holds one entry afterwards and the neighbourhood is one
unverified_bad_case: the bucket degrades only with many drops that are close AND cannot merge, i.e. differing item, components or stack cap. No fixture exercises that yet.
open_question: environment is 178.8ms (53 percent) of entity_heavy, about 298us per xp orb, which is far too high for a mutex lock. keepalive_time_tick also runs crop growth, which calls set_block with occlusion, batching and invalidation. Not isolated.
next: split keepalive_time_tick into separate stages so the environment cost can be attributed
review: NOT RUN, external usage limit still in force
